entities.summary: Zelda Popkin was an American novelist best known for her contributions to mid-twentieth-century detective fiction and her later works exploring Jewish identity and family life. Over a career spanning four decades, she wrote fourteen books, including seven mystery novels and several works of general fiction. She gained early recognition for creating Mary Carner, a department-store detective who debuted in Death Wears a White Gardenia (1938) and is regarded by scholars as one of the first professionally competent female sleuths to appear in American popular fiction.
